skill.name: daily-news-report
skill.description: Collects technical news from configured public sources, filters for quality and duplicates, and writes a daily Markdown report with source links.
skill.summary: Create a daily technical news brief from curated public sources.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most external command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline documentation, not executable shell calls. Confirmed risks are intentional external network requests to public sources, plus semantic risks from untrusted web content and browser-rendered pages.

remediation.issue: Untrusted web content is summarized by agents without explicit prompt-injection handling.
remediation.suggestion: Add instructions that scraped page text is untrusted data and must not override system, developer, or user instructions.

remediation.issue: The workflow opens third-party JavaScript pages through browser tooling.
remediation.suggestion: Run browser scraping in an isolated session without user credentials, and close pages after extraction.

remediation.issue: External network requests are part of normal execution.
remediation.suggestion: Document the enabled domain allowlist and require user confirmation before fetching newly added sources.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Web Content Can Influence Agent Output
semantic_findings.description: The workflow sends scraped public pages to agents and asks them to return structured results. No explicit guard tells agents to ignore instructions embedded inside page content.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited task prompts show external content extraction and strict output requests, but no prompt-injection boundary for scraped text. This is a common risk for summarization workflows.

semantic_findings.title: Third-Party JavaScript Pages Are Rendered in Browser Tooling
semantic_findings.description: The workflow opens JavaScript-rendered third-party pages through Chrome DevTools and parses browser snapshots. This can expose browser state if the session is not isolated.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly call Chrome DevTools operations on ProductHunt, Latent Space, and other SPA pages. I did not find isolation or credential-state guidance.

content.value_statement: Technical teams need a concise way to track useful articles, papers, and product updates. This skill collects curated sources, filters duplicates, and creates a Markdown brief.
actual_capabilities: Reads source priorities and fetch methods from sources.json.
Collects items from configured public technical and productivity sources.
Uses staged batches and optional browser rendering for difficult pages.
Scores, deduplicates, and selects high-quality items for the report.
Generates a dated Markdown report in the NewsReport directory.
Updates cache data to reduce repeated collection across runs.
limitations: Requires network access to public websites listed in the configuration.
Source availability, paywalls, and site layout changes can reduce quality.
Browser scraping requires a compatible Chrome DevTools MCP tool.
It does not independently verify every claim in scraped articles.

use_cases.title: Prepare Team News Briefs
use_cases.description: Create a daily technical digest that engineering or product teams can scan quickly.

use_cases.title: Track AI Research Updates
use_cases.description: Collect notable papers, tools, and deep technical discussions from configured AI sources.

use_cases.title: Build Personal Reading Queues
use_cases.description: Generate a focused Markdown list of articles with summaries, links, keywords, and quality scores.

prompt_templates.title: Run Today Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate today's daily news report using the configured sources. Save the report with today's date.

prompt_templates.title: Run Date Specific Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a report for a specific day
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a daily news report for 2026-07-08. Use the cache to avoid repeated items where possible.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize AI Sources
prompt_templates.scenario: Focus on AI and deep technology content
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a daily report with priority on AI research, developer tools, and deep technology. Exclude general productivity posts unless they are highly actionable.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Source Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate the report, then summarize source success rates, skipped sources, duplicate counts, and recommendations for updating sources.json.

output_examples.input: Generate today's report from the default source list.
output_examples.output: A Markdown report with a dated title, collection statistics, twenty ranked items, summaries, source links, keywords, and generation metadata.

output_examples.input: Focus the report on AI research and developer tools.
output_examples.output: A filtered brief that favors papers, technical posts, and practical tools while excluding low-value marketing and job posts.

output_examples.input: Review source performance after report generation.
output_examples.output: A concise operational note covering successful sources, failed sources, duplicate counts, browser fallback use, and cache updates.

best_practices: Review sources.json before scheduled runs so only trusted sources are enabled.
Check the generated report for source quality before sharing it with a team.
Keep cache.json available between runs to reduce duplicates and repeated fetching.
anti_patterns: Do not enable unknown websites without reviewing their content and fetch requirements.
Do not treat scraped summaries as verified facts without checking the original sources.
Do not run browser scraping in a session that contains sensitive logged-in state.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It generates a daily Markdown news report from configured technical and productivity sources.

faq.question: Can I change the sources?
faq.answer: Yes. Update sources.json to add, disable, or reprioritize sources before running the workflow.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: Yes. It fetches public websites and may use browser rendering for JavaScript-heavy pages.

faq.question: How does it reduce duplicate articles?
faq.answer: It compares URLs, checks title similarity, and uses cache history to avoid repeated items.

faq.question: Can it work without a worker agent?
faq.answer: Yes. The instructions describe a serial fallback mode when a worker agent is unavailable.

faq.question: Is every article fact checked?
faq.answer: No. The report summarizes source content, so important claims should be verified at the source.
